shared_context.content: Throughout, \mathbb{N} = \{1,2,3,\dots\}. A function g: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} takes positive integer values. For a real number r and positive integer m, the expression m^r is the usual real power.
shared_context.label: Natural-number convention

shared_context.content: For a function g: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}, define d_n := g(n+1)-g(n) for n \in \mathbb{N}. If g satisfies g(n+1)-g(n) \ge (g(g(n)))^r for all n and r \ge 0, then each d_n is a positive integer.
shared_context.label: Difference-sequence convention

strategy_summary: Reformulate the problem through the difference sequence d_n := g(n+1)-g(n). Prove the lower bound by the explicit quadratic construction g(n)=n^2. For the upper bound, first show any admissible function is strictly increasing, hence the difference sequence is positive and nondecreasing when r>0. Then derive a structural lower bound g(g(n)) \ge (g(n)-1)^2/n from monotone averages of the differences. This converts the original inequality into a growth inequality for d_n in terms of g(n). A dedicated impossibility lemma shows that these coupled monotonicity and growth constraints force r \le 1/4. The theorem then follows by combining the explicit witness at r=1/4 with the impossibility of any witness for r>1/4.
